answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to stake reputation earned through verifiable work history recorded in a shared atlas of attestations. New identities start hollow: no past jobs, no peer endorsements, no stake to lose. Each completed task adds a signed signal to the atlas — who hired the agent, what was delivered, whether payment cleared. Attackers can spin up thousands of hollow identities, but each one must buy its way into trust with real, costly work before it can take high-value jobs, so flooding the market costs more than it earns.
